promise: We will achieve annual GDP growth of 4 percent
description: AMLO repeatedly promised that his government would deliver 4% annual GDP growth, making it a central claim of his 'Fourth Transformation'. Growth averaged only about 1% per year across his six-year term (2019-2024, including the -8% COVID crash of 2020), making it one of the most-cited unfulfilled promises of his presidency.
evidence: IMF's October 2024 assessment records 2021 GDP growth of 6.0%, so growth did exceed 4% in one year.
Assessing an average-term 4% pledge requires a consistent series, not a claim that no single year exceeded it.

review.note: IMF's 2024 table reports 6.0% growth in 2021, refuting 'no year reached 4%'. Original pledge and consistent final term-average remain unverified; 2024 data here are projections, not final outturn.

promise: Disney targeted 60-90 million Disney+ subscribers by the end of fiscal 2024.
description: Disney's April 11, 2019 forecast was exceeded numerically: fiscal-2024 results reported 122.7 million Disney+ Core subscribers and 35.9 million Hotstar subscribers.
evidence: The investor-day material gives the 60-90 million fiscal-2024 target.
Official results give the September 28, 2024 period end and separate Core and Hotstar counts.

promise: We expect Disney+ to reach 230 million to 260 million paid subscribers by fiscal 2024 (as reported).
description: Disney ended fiscal 2024 with 122.7 million Disney+ Core subscribers and 35.9 million Hotstar subscribers, or 158.6 million combined, below the stated 230-260 million target.
evidence: Disney's FY2024 results separate Core and Hotstar counts.

review.note: FY2024 figures were 122.7m core plus 35.9m Hotstar, totaling 158.6m, not 150m core. Compare like scope to original target; original investor-day attribution/timestamp still needs source.

person: United Nations member states (Pact for the Future)
promise: Adopt the Pact for the Future at the Summit of the Future in September 2024
description: Following the September 1, 2023 modalities decision 77/568, the General Assembly adopted the Pact for the Future on September 22, 2024, together with the Global Digital Compact and Declaration on Future Generations. Adoption fulfilled this procedural commitment; it does not establish implementation of every measure.
evidence: The Pact and its two annexes were adopted on September 22, 2024.
sources: United Nations: Pact for the Future adopted

promise: Cut Games carbon emissions by 50% compared with the London 2012 and Rio 2016 average
description: Paris 2024's final sustainability report estimates the Games' carbon footprint at 1.595 million tonnes CO2e, 54.6% below the average of London 2012 and Rio 2016. This exceeds its halving target on the organizer's stated accounting basis; the claim is not carbon neutrality.
evidence: Final Paris 2024 emissions reported at about 1.6 Mt CO2e, ~54% below the London/Rio average
London 2012 was estimated at 3.3 Mt and Rio 2016 at 3.6 Mt
CBC reported the Games cut carbon by over half compared with 2012 and 2016

review.note: Organizer's final assessment reports 1.595 million tonnes CO2e and a 54.6% reduction against the London/Rio average, supporting the target on its stated accounting basis. It is not proof of carbon neutrality. Exact September 13, 2017 announcement date was not established.
